## Central Limit Theorem (Quantitative Data)

```{r}
set.seed(123) # because we want to reproduce our randomness

pop <- rexp(n = 100000) # exponential distribution

# look up sample()

simulate_clt <- function(population, n, num_sim, stat){
 results <- NA
 
 for (i in 1:num_sim){
   sample_data <- sample(population, n)
   results[i] <- stat(sample_data)
 }
   return(results)
}

mean_values <- simulate_clt(pop, 30, 5000, mean)

hist(pop)

hist(mean_values)
```

#### Simulated Discovery 

YOU discovered that the CLT doesn't work with ordered statistics (like the max, min, etc) via simulation!

```{r}
max_values <- simulate_clt(pop, 30, 5000, max)

hist(pop)

hist(max_values)
```


## Central Limit Theorem (Categorical Data)

```{r}
pop <- c(rep(0, 3000), rep(1, 7000))

mean_values <- simulate_clt(pop, 30, 5000, mean)

hist(pop)

hist(mean_values)
```

The CLT does work with proportions when we do have enough successes and failures!
